cards.text: Babylon's army has Jerusalem surrounded, and Jeremiah the prophet just bought a field from his cousin (Jeremiah 32:2, 9). That's like buying a beach house while the hurricane's already on the porch. Now Jeremiah gives the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, who was told to keep it in a clay jar for a long time (Jeremiah 32:14), and he prays to the LORD.

cards.question: Jeremiah opens his prayer with “Oh, Lord GOD!” What does he say God made by His great power and outstretched arm?
After praising God for making the heavens and the earth, Jeremiah says a few things are still too difficult for God.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah tells God who He is: the One who shows loving devotion to thousands but lays the iniquity of the fathers into the laps of their children after them, the great and mighty God whose name is the LORD of Hosts. Babylon's army is OUTSIDE, friend, and this man is taking his time with the praise.

cards.question: Jeremiah calls God great in counsel and mighty in deed, with His eyes on all the ways of people. What are His eyes on them for?

answers.text: To reward each one by his ways
To find the ones He can trust
To keep count of every name

cards.text: Now Jeremiah walks back through history. God did signs and wonders in Egypt and brought His people out with a strong hand and an outstretched arm.

cards.question: After God brings His people out of Egypt, what does Jeremiah say God gives them?

answers.text: The land He swore to their fathers
A king to lead them into battle
A city with high stone walls

cards.text: They come in and possess the land, promise kept. Now, friend... what do they do with it?

cards.question: Once Israel possessed the land, Jeremiah says they obeyed God's voice and walked in His law.
Because Israel didn't do what God commanded, Jeremiah says God brought all this ___ on them.

cards.text: Jeremiah points at what's happening right now. Siege ramps are up against the city, and by sword, famine and plague it has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans, the Babylonians fighting against it.

cards.question: Looking at the siege, Jeremiah tells God that what He had spoken has happened.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah lands on the field: the city's already delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans, and God still told him to BUY it. Friend, I'd have read that order twice.

cards.question: Even with the city handed over to the Chaldeans, Jeremiah reminds God what He said about the field. Besides buying it with silver, what did God tell him to do?

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah, and the God of all flesh asks, “Is anything too difficult for Me?” Friend, He made a worn-out stamper from the back of a junk drawer brand new, so I'm gonna go ahead and say NO.
God says He's about to deliver this city into the hands of the Chaldeans and of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, who will capture it.

cards.question: God says the Chaldeans fighting against Jerusalem will come in. Then what will they do to the city?

answers.text: Set it on fire and burn it
Leave it standing and go home

cards.question: God says some of the houses that will burn in Jerusalem belong to people who provoked Him to anger. What did they do?

cards.text: God says the children of Israel and of Judah have done nothing but evil in His sight from their youth. This city has stirred up His wrath and fury from the day it was built until now.

cards.question: Jerusalem has stirred up God's wrath since the day it was built. So what does God say He will do with it?
God says the evil came from the common people, while the kings, priests and prophets stayed faithful.

cards.text: God says He taught them again and again. And still they would not listen or respond to discipline.

cards.question: God says His people have turned their ___ to Him and not their faces.
God keeps going. Where does He say His people placed their abominations and defiled it?

answers.text: In the house that bears His Name
In the courtyard of the palace
Beside the gates of the city

cards.text: In the Valley of Ben-hinnom they built high places of Baal, a false god, to make their sons and daughters pass through the fire to Molech, another false god.

cards.question: God says this abomination in the Valley of Ben-hinnom was something He never commanded, and it never entered His mind.

cards.text: Now God turns to the city “of which you say, ‘It will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon by sword and famine and plague…’” And friend, listen to what He says next.

cards.question: God has named the city's fall to Babylon. What does He say He will surely do with the people He has banished?

answers.text: Gather them from all the lands
Leave them in Babylon for good

cards.text: He'll return them to this place and make them dwell in safety. After years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, nobody has to explain to ME how good that sounds.

cards.question: God promises that they will be His people, and He will be their God.
God says He will give His people one heart and one way. What will that lead them to do?

answers.text: Always fear Him for their good
Rebuild the walls of the city

cards.text: Then God says He will make an everlasting covenant with them. He will never turn away from doing good to them.

cards.question: God also says He'll put His fear in His people's hearts. What will that keep them from doing?

cards.text: And here's the part that gets me. God says He will rejoice in doing them good, and He'll faithfully plant them in this land with all His heart and all His soul.

cards.question: God says that after all this great disaster, He will bring on His people only part of the good He promised them.

cards.text: Then God talks about the land that's being called a desolation, without man or beast, handed over to the Chaldeans.

cards.question: In the land being called a desolation, God says ___ will be bought.

cards.text: Fields will be purchased with silver, and deeds signed, sealed and witnessed, from the land of Benjamin to the cities of Judah. Jeremiah's field wasn't a bad deal, friend, he was just EARLY!

cards.question: Fields and deeds all over the land again. Why does God say it will happen?

answers.text: He will restore them from captivity
Babylon will lose interest in the land
The people will earn the land back
